clauses.reason: First end: express revocation on 1934-10-12. EO 6871 paragraph 1 provides 'That paragraph numbered 1 of Executive Order No. 6861, dated September 28, 1934, be and it is hereby revoked.' Actor: EO 6871. The stay's own stated end was October 15, 1934 (inclusive; exclusive reading: when that day began), later than the revocation. EO 6871 paragraph 2 then stays the same amendments to and including December 1, 1934 by its own command; that is a later event, not an extension of this stay.

Exhausted by performance on 1934-10-10. EO 6871's recital states that the Board 'duly appointed' the three named persons as the committee under this order and that the committee 'on October 10, 1934, did report its recommendations' after hearing protests and investigating; the command (appoint forthwith, hear, report on or before October 10, 1934) was fully performed on the report date, with the appointment falling between September 28 and October 10. Actor: the National Industrial Recovery Board and its committee, as recited by EO 6871. EO 6871 paragraph 3 continues the committee with new instructions on its own authority; that is a later event, not a continuation of this command.

Exhausted by performance no later than 1934-10-12. EO 6871, dated October 12, 1934, recites the committee's report of October 10 and states 'I ... do hereby approve and adopt the report and recommendations of said committee', so the recommendations had reached the President by October 12; the transmittal therefore occurred between October 10 and October 12, 1934. The exact day is not stated; the clause is dated at the day by which the evidence shows performance. The order does not say that the Board itself carried the document; the command's object, that the recommendations reach the President, was accomplished. Actor as recited: the Board.

inventory_overrides.reason: Paragraph 1, the stay of the amendments to Articles III and IV up to and including October 15, 1934. The machine's 'lead' (the authority recital and 'I hereby order:') commands nothing by itself and is dropped; each numbered paragraph is its own command.
Paragraph 2, the direction to the National Industrial Recovery Board to appoint a committee of three that hears the protests and reports by October 10, 1934.

Paragraph 3, the direction to the Board to transmit the committee's recommendations to the President. The trailing 'understanding' sentence (that the protestants will abide by the President's decision) states the basis on which the order was made and commands no one, so it is excluded.

research_rationale:
Text and identity: EO 6861 is read in full in the registered American Presidency Project (APP) transcription jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6861-staying-certain-amendments-the-code-fair-competition-for-the-cotton.txt (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-29: the row with the same sha256 (1369a32ed467...) in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl is a common-crawl capture (CC-MAIN-2024-42, captured 2024-10-15T03:46:11Z, WARC location recorded so the page can be re-fetched) whose heading is 'Executive Order 6861—Staying Certain Amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Garment Industry Approved by Executive Order No. 6828 of August 21, 1934' and whose date is 1934-09-28; that date agrees with the date line of the held text ('September 28, 1934.'), and the row's text_sha256 equals the held file's. The held file is the whole order (recital, operative paragraph, signature, the Administrator's recommendation and the date line); it carries no order number, so the number comes from the page record. Clauses and sources are quoted from this registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. Identity: number, date and subject agree across the APP page record, the census register ('Executive Order 6861—Staying Certain Amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Garment Industry Approved by Executive Order No. 6828 of August 21, 1934', 1934-09-28) and the WPA 1944 numbered list (printed page 592: 'Effectivedate of amendments to ArticlesIII and IV of the Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Garment Industry stayed untilOct. 15, 1934, and the National IndustrialRecovery Board ordered to appoint a committee of three to hear protestsagainst said amendments. XVII NRA Codes 523.'). The WPA list says the order stays the effective date of amendments to Articles III and IV of the Cotton Garment Code until October 15, 1934 and orders the Board to appoint a committee of three (XVII NRA Codes 523). The later order EO 6871 (the revoking order) is also page-checked: its APP page record (node 362578, common-crawl capture 2025-03-23) has the heading 'Executive Order 6871', date 1934-10-12 as in the text's date line, and a text_sha256 equal to the held file's. EO 6861 (September 28, 1934, Franklin D. Roosevelt), made 'in order to effectuate the purposes of said title', orders: (1) that the amendments to Articles III and IV of the Cotton Garment Code approved by EO 6828 'be stayed up to and including October 15, 1934'; (2) that the National Industrial Recovery Board 'shall forthwith appoint a committee of three impartial persons' who will 'hear said protests, investigate the facts and report its recommendations on or before October 10, 1934'; (3) that the Board 'shall immediately transmit said recommendations to me'. This is a mixed order, so each command has its own end. The machine inventory (a lead plus three items) is corrected to the three commands. Clause 1 (the stay): EO 6871 (October 12, 1934), paragraph 1, orders 'That paragraph numbered 1 of Executive Order No. 6861 ... be and it is hereby revoked.' The first end is that revocation on 1934-10-12, three days before the stay's own stated end (October 15, inclusive; exclusive reading: when October 15 began). EO 6871 paragraph 2 stays the same amendments to and including December 1, 1934; that is a separate new stay by the later order, recorded as a later event, not an extension of this stay (the stay and the revocation are express, so the strike-and-insert and further-exemption rulings do not turn the revocation into an amendment). Clause 2 (committee): EO 6871 recites that the Board 'pursuant to said Executive Order duly appointed Willard E. Hotchkiss, W. Jett Lauck and Donald M. Nelson ... as such committee, which said committee thereafter heard protests, investigated the facts and on October 10, 1934, did report its recommendations'. The command (appoint, hear, report by October 10) was performed and is exhausted on 1934-10-10, the date of the report; the appointment fell between September 28 and October 10. EO 6871 paragraph 3 continues the committee with new instructions on its own authority, which is a later event of the committee, not a continuation of this command. Clause 3 (transmittal): EO 6871 states that the President 'do[es] hereby approve and adopt the report and recommendations of said committee' on October 12, 1934, so the recommendations had reached him by then; the report was made on October 10. The transmittal was therefore made between October 10 and October 12, 1934. The exact day is not stated; the clause is dated 1934-10-12, the day by which the evidence shows performance, and the interval is stated. The order does not state that the Board itself carried the document, only that the recommendations had reached the President; that is the object of the command.

The name search found EO 6828 (the approval whose amendments are stayed), EO 6871 (the revocation and re-stay) and nothing else naming this order; no other held order revokes, shortens or extends it. Searches made on 2026-10-29: (1) a full-text search of every held order text numbered 6200 through 7100 under jobs/*/output/texts (APP, HathiTrust GPO, Wikisource and Federal Register texts; clause-drafts copies excluded) for the code's name; (2) a citation search of the same texts for this order's number; (3) a search of the same texts for general NRA orders that could suspend, cancel or supersede codes: the held general orders (EO 6354 as amended by EO 6710, EO 6646, 6711, 6750-C, 6764 and 6829) prescribe rules, contract terms and delegations, and none suspends, cancels or supersedes the code named here; (4) the census register titles (jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv) and the WPA 1944 numbered list, read for this code's name; they show no cancellation, suspension or superseding code. savings.reason: The stay's effect (the Article III and IV amendments did not operate from their original date until EO 6871's stay ended on December 1, 1934), the committee's report of October 10, 1934 and the President's adoption of it on October 12, 1934 are accrued, completed effects. Nothing in EO 6861 continues any command after October 12, 1934; EO 6871 stayed the amendments again and continued the committee by its own commands.

source_notes.reason: NIRA section 3(a)-(f): the legal effects of a code approval that the repeal removed (3(a) approval and conditions, 3(b) standards of fair competition, 3(c) injunction suits, 3(f) misdemeanor).
